clauses.reason: The paragraph appoints William C. Strand as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice James P. Davis, resigned, and its last sentence amends Executive Orders 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689 accordingly. Both are one-time acts performed when the order was signed on 1953-07-07, so the clause was spent on that date; the order has no effective-date wording and no later date applies. The appointee's continued service and the earlier orders as amended are surviving consequences and not commands of this order. No later order is held that amends, revokes or extends it.

research_rationale:
EO 10468 (signed 1953-07-07 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1953-07-07, 4:09 p.m.; 18 FR 3979, Federal Register of July 9, 1953 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10468.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one operative paragraph and one closing sentence. The paragraph appoints William C. Strand, Director, Office of Territories, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice James P. Davis, resigned, to serve without additional compensation and to exercise and discharge the functions, duties and authority that Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689 conferred on the Administration and its Administrator. The closing sentence amends those orders accordingly. There is no deadline, sunset or condition. First end: both commands are one-time acts. The appointment was made, and the amendments to the earlier orders took effect, when the order was signed; the text has no effective-date wording, so the signing date 1953-07-07 is recorded (the filing date is the same day). What survives is a consequence of the performed appointment and not a continuing command of this order: Strand's holding of the office and the earlier orders as amended. The functions he exercises come from Executive Orders 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689, not from this order. No held source shows when Strand left the office or when the Administration ended. A contents line in the held Federal Register text printed with EO 10597 (issue of 1955-02-17) lists an Interior Department notice on cessation of functions and activities of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration at 20 FR 1027; the notice itself is not held. Those facts concern the surviving appointment and the earlier orders, not whether this order's own commands were performed. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10468 found only the order's own copies and a page number in another document; a scan of held order texts numbered above 10468 for the Administration's name and for Strand's name found no order. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts). I also adopted the held-text person-name search, which found no hit for the appointee.

savings.reason: The appointment of Strand and the amendments to Executive Orders 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689 are performed acts whose consequences continue independently of any command left in this order: the appointment stands as the act that placed Strand in the office until his service ended, and the earlier orders stand as amended. The order contains no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. The end of Strand's service and of the Administration is not shown by a held source and is not needed to fix when this order's own commands were performed.
